title: fix(app-shell): the flow inspector's inline visibleWhen cell for a screen field reads the screen's declared fields, as the Problems panel and the Debug run do (objectui#10772)
body:
Fixes #10772
Clause-②: no — a Studio authoring hint moves onto the already-ruled screen scope (ruling C on objectui#10743); no declared surface moves

Executes the triage direction on objectui#10772 (comment 5856191354, from ruling C `5853038135` on objectui#10743) under claim 5856807565. Branch `claude/issue-10772-inline-cell-screen-scope`, head `b6e912aab4`, base `29b45f6a0c`. Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 2, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`.

## What changed

- `inspectors/FlowObjectListField.tsx`: the `expression` column branch asks `screenVisibleWhenNode(context.node, fieldId, col.key)`. When that names a screen node, the picker gets `screenScopeGroups(node)`: one "Screen fields" section holding exactly `[...screenPredicateRoots(node)]`, which is the screen's declared fields plus `record`. `FlowExprIssue` gets `screenNode`. Every other expression column is unchanged and keeps `scopeGroups`, the flow scope. New optional prop `fieldId`: the list's descriptor id. It is never forwarded to a nested list, so a nested list can never qualify.
- `inspectors/FlowExprIssue.tsx`: new optional prop `screenNode`. When it is set, the unknown-reference step is `screenVisibleWhenScopeError(value, screenNode)`, and `scopeGroups` is not read. The brace/shape error still comes first (`validateExpressionClient`), in the Problems panel's order (`checkScreenVisibleWhen`). The docblock now says which scope each cell reads (direction item 2).
- `inspectors/FlowNodeConfigField.tsx` (the plumbing): passes `fieldId={field.id}` to `FlowObjectListField`. One prop, plus a comment.
- `previews/flow-expr-problems.ts`: `isScreenVisibleWhenColumn` is now `export`ed, with its docblock saying why. The cell names the column with the same predicate the Problems panel uses, so the column's identity is not copied. ⚠ This file was not in the claimed file surface. It is declared here: one keyword, and no verdict moves.
- `inspectors/flow-scope.ts`: `ScopeGroupId` gains `'screen_fields'`. This follows the approval precedent: its own id, so the section can never leak into the flow picker. The change is type-only.
- `previews/screen-spec.ts`: read-only. No export was needed; `screenPredicateRoots` and `screenVisibleWhenScopeError` were already exported.
- `.changeset/10743-studio-screen-visiblewhen-live.md`: a dated note (objectui#10533 form) follows its "Still on the flow scope" paragraph. That paragraph is kept as the record of that change. Frontmatter md5 of lines 1–3 is `4e8ce55021fe3b14329c8b4cb3f9f354` before and after.
- `packages/app-shell/README.md`: the flows paragraph said "the inline inspector's `visibleWhen` cell still reads the flow scope (a follow-up)". This change makes that sentence false, and the README is published (`files` lists `README.md`), so it now says the cell follows the same rule. Declared as a file-surface addition.
- `.changeset/10772-inline-screen-visiblewhen-cell.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## H1: reproduced on base `29b45f6a0c`

Probe (not committed): the real `FlowObjectListField` with the `screen` descriptor's `fields` columns, `context` set to the draft and node, and the `resolveFlowScope` groups. The draft has a `record-after-update` start on `crm_lead`, a flow variable `needsApproval`, and a screen `review`. Readings, verbatim:

- tokens offered: `["needsApproval","record","previous"]`
- `note`, `discount > 0` (sibling): NOTES `["`discount` is not a reference in scope at this step."]`
- `other`, `other_field == 'x'`: NOTES `["`other_field` is not a reference in scope at this step."]`
- `reason`, `needsApproval == true` (run variable): NOTES `[]`
- PICKER (option text is token then detail): `["needsApprovalvariable · boolean","recordtrigger record · crm_lead","previousrecord values before the change"]`

The card's measurement holds on base.

## H2: the seam

- The cell is the `col.kind === 'expression'` branch of `FlowObjectListField`. Before this change it rendered `VariableTextInput groups={scopeGroups ?? []}` and `FlowExprIssue scopeGroups={scopeGroups}`, and `FlowExprIssue` ran `findUnknownRefs(value, role, scopeRoots(groups))`.
- The node was already there: `FlowNodeInspector` passes `context={{ draft, node }}` through `FlowNodeConfigField` into `FlowObjectListField`. The field id was missing. The Problems panel names the column by `isScreenVisibleWhenColumn(type, fieldId, colKey)`, so the one missing input is `fieldId`, set by `FlowNodeConfigField` from `field.id`.
- The function is `screenVisibleWhenNode(context.node, fieldId, col.key)`, which returns a `ScreenPreviewNode` or `undefined`. It feeds `screenScopeGroups(node)`, which is `screenPredicateRoots(node)`, for the picker, and `FlowExprIssue.screenNode` (`screenVisibleWhenScopeError(value, node)`) for the note. No third copy of the rule.
- What `screenVisibleWhenScopeError` returns for `needsApproval == true` on this screen is the sentence "`needsApproval` is not a field on this screen". No nearest-field suffix is added, because no declared field is close. The Problems panel shows the same sentence prefixed by the row label ("Reason: …"). The inline cell sits in the row, so it shows the sentence without a prefix. The pin asserts equality with the panel's message instead of pinning the literal.

## Pins and ablation

New file `inspectors/FlowObjectListField.screenVisibleWhen-10772.test.tsx`. It mounts through the real plumbing: `FlowNodeConfigField` with the real `screen` and `decision` descriptors, `context` set to the draft and node, and `resolveFlowScope` groups.

1. A sibling-field predicate is silent: `discount > 0` and `other_field == 'x'` (both declared on the screen) show no note and no alert.
2. A run variable is flagged in the Problems panel's words. The `needsApproval == true` cell shows exactly one `role="note"` naming `needsApproval`. The panel's messages on node `review` equal `["Reason: " + that note]`, at `warning`.
3. The picker offers the screen roots: the tokens equal `[...screenPredicateRoots(review)]` (`discount`, `other_field`, `note`, `extra`, `reason`, `record`), with no `needsApproval` and no `previous`.
4. Control, a decision's `conditions[].expression` upstream of the screen: `discount > 0` is flagged naming `discount`, `needsApproval == true` is clean, and the picker equals the `resolveFlowScope` tokens (`needsApproval`, `record`, `previous`).

- Red leg: the five base sources were checked out from `29b45f6a0c` under the head pin file, with blobs confirmed equal to base. The restore was trap-driven with `git checkout HEAD --`, every blob was re-checked equal to HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` was empty afterwards. Result: `Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4)`. Pins 1–3 are red; control 4 is green.
- Green leg at `b6e912aab4`: `Tests 4 passed (4)`.
- Ablation (flow-scope fallback) ran through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. It replaced `const screenNode = screenVisibleWhenNode(context?.node, fieldId, col.key);` with `const screenNode: ScreenPreviewNode | undefined = undefined;`. The anchor hit exactly once and went from 1 to 0 hits; the blob went from `599051a346e0` to `da61329c536d`. Run over the pin file plus the three existing `FlowObjectListField.*` suites: `Test Files 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`, `Tests 3 failed | 11 passed (14)`. Only the three screen pins are red; the control and every existing row stay green. The restore left the blob equal to HEAD `599051a346e0` and `git diff HEAD` empty, and afterwards the marker count on disk is 0 and the anchor count is 1.

## Gates (at `b6e912aab4`, every run of the heavy ones under the verify lock; seconds are shared-box)

- Dependency closure `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: the script echoed `@object-ui/app-shell@17.6.0 type-check`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new pin file (1 hit).
- Tests, narrowed to the 24 test files that import a touched module (`git grep` over app-shell tests for imports of `FlowExprIssue`, `FlowObjectListField`, `FlowNodeConfigField`, `FlowKeyValueField`, `FlowNodeInspector`, `flow-scope`, `useFlowScope`, `flow-expr-problems`): `Test Files 24 passed (24)`, `Tests 299 passed (299)`. This narrowing is declared. Tests that reach these modules only transitively are not in that set; the full `pnpm test` is CI's run.
- eslint on the six changed source and test files (`--format json`): 6 files, 0 errors, 1 warning. The warning is `react-hooks/refs` on the `rows.map` line of `FlowObjectListField.tsx`, and it is pre-existing: the base blob linted alone shows the same rule, 1 warning. `eslint.config.js` has no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService` and no type-checked preset (0 hits), and no import-resolution plugin. So type-aware linting is off, and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-level `pnpm lint` is CI's run.
- `check-changeset-presence` ✅ (9 files changed, 6 published source, 1 changeset added). `check-control-bytes` ✅. `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`: `VERDICT … 0 new citation(s)`. `check-pending-changeset-literals` ✅. `check-changeset-no-major` ✅. `check-changeset-fixed` ✅. `check-vi-mock-specifiers` ✅. `check-vi-mock-override-shape` ✅. `check-vi-mock-inherit` ✅. `check-test-path-roots` ✅.
- `check-changeset-claims` (report-only) names two pending changesets that cite `flow-scope.ts`: `6296-conditionbuilder-subject-vocabulary.md` and `flow-entry-condition-builder.md`. Both paragraphs are still true. They describe `fieldPrefix: onStart ? '' : 'record.'` and `includePrevious`, and that text reads 1 and 5 occurrences at both base and head. This diff adds one union member and a comment to `ScopeGroupId` and nothing else.
- `check-changeset-overwrite` (report-only) records the modification of `10743-studio-screen-visiblewhen-live.md`, case 2: a deliberate prose correction with the declaration unchanged (`@object-ui/app-shell: patch` at base and now).

- NOT MEASURED: `check-readme-exports`, because app-shell's own `dist` is not built here (only its dependency closure). The README edit is prose inside an existing bullet and adds no fenced import block. CI's README Export Check covers it. Console Performance Budget (eager closure) is CI's.

## Serial

The claim read open PRs at 14:25Z and none touched these files. Before the last push, `origin/main` was fetched into the private ref `refs/issue-10772/main` at `bff63cc12e` (3 commits and 47 files past base). `git merge-tree --write-tree` against HEAD exited 0 (tree `13994de4a0`). The intersection of main's moved files with this PR's 9 files is empty, and none of main's moved files is under `metadata-admin/inspectors/`, `metadata-admin/previews/` or `ScreenView`.

## Acceptance notes

- The screen roots are read from the committed node (`context.node.config.fields`), the same node the Problems panel judges. A field row renamed in the cell is picked up on that row's flush, on blur or Enter, not keystroke by keystroke.
- The "Screen fields" section offers `record` as a bare token, because `screenPredicateRoots` admits it (`record.discount` resolves as `discount` does). The section carries no per-token detail, since the rule yields names only.
- Carried over from the objectui#10743 review, not new and not addressed here: `record.zzz > 0` is clean on every surface (the root `record` is admitted) while the runner faults on it. The inline cell now inherits that same reading. objectui#10743 remains closed as delivered.
- "Screen fields" is an English literal, like the picker's other section labels in `useFlowScope` ("Flow variables", "Trigger record"). The screen sentence is the Problems panel's English literal, and the flow wording is localized, as recorded on objectui#10743.
- The server half, where `registerFlow` and the resume door narrow to the declared scope, is objectstack-ai/objectstack#20178. It is unchanged by this PR.
